report.verdict: A volume-led quarter from an unlisted B2B supplier that discloses growth rates, not money: sportsbook GGR +33.4% YoY on actives +82.7% and bets +31.9% means GGR per active fell ~27% (our arithmetic) — breadth from new operator go-lives and World Cup/Esports World Cup casuals, not deeper monetisation. Growth has decelerated from +61% in Q1 and +42.7% in H1 but re-accelerated versus an implied ~+24% Q2 (est.), while lapping a soft-hold September 2025 comp. With no revenue, EBITDA, handle, hold, partner-count or concentration disclosure, this is a momentum signal, not an underwritable result.

summary: **What this is — and is not.** BETBY (legal entity Earlybird Ltd, Malta reg. C 94530; MGA B2B licence MGA/B2B/780/2020, issued 3 Aug 2020; founded 2018) is privately held and unlisted. The 29 Oct 2026 'Q3 results' is a voluntary trading update giving YoY percentage KPIs only — no revenue, GGR base, NGR, EBITDA, net income, EPS, cash or debt. There is no exchange filing, no call transcript and no guidance. Every monetary line in this note is therefore n/a (not estimated); the analysis is of operating momentum. Fiscal year-end 31 Dec is inferred from the calendar-quarter reporting cadence, not from filings.

**Headline: sportsbook GGR +33.4% YoY**, total bets placed +31.9%, active players +82.7% across the partner network (company release; corroborated by Gaming.net, Yogonet, Focus GN, SBC News, G3). No consensus exists, so 'vs expectations' is not measurable.

**Decomposition says volume, not monetisation.** GGR grew in line with bet count (GGR per bet ~+1%) while actives grew ~2.5x faster than GGR: implied GGR per active ~-27% and bets per active ~-28% (our arithmetic). The incremental Q3 player is lower-frequency and lower-value — consistent with new operator go-lives and event-driven casual acquisition rather than deeper engagement of the existing base.

**Sharp flip in the shape of growth vs 2025.** In Q3-25 the same KPIs were GGR +56.07%, bets +24.92%, actives +19.45% (GGR per active +31%, GGR per bet +25%) — stake/hold-led. H1-26 was transitional (GGR +42.7%, bets +21.2%, actives +47%; GGR per bet +18%, GGR per active -3%). Q3-26 is the first period where per-player economics are clearly diluting.

**Trajectory: decelerating, but off the Q2 trough.** Sportsbook GGR growth went +61% (Q1-26, record March) → +42.7% (H1-26) → +33.4% (Q3-26). Q2 standalone is not published; equal-weighting the Q1/Q2-25 bases implies Q2-26 at ~+24% (range ~20–30% depending on base weights; est.), so Q3 is a modest re-acceleration. Two-year Q3 stack ~+108%.

**Comp quality flatters Q3.** The Q3-25 release flagged lower sportsbook margins in September 2025 from unfavourable sporting results; some of the +33.4% is hold normalisation rather than volume. The company discloses no handle, hold or NGR, so luck vs structural cannot be split. Nor was the Q3-25 base event-free: they cited a 743% GGR surge in pre-match markets during the FIFA Club World Cup (final 13 Jul 2025).

**Event stats: qualitative only.** Management credited the Esports World Cup and the concluding stages of the FIFA World Cup (knockout rounds to the 19 Jul final; the group stage sat in Q2). No World Cup GGR, handle, actives or margin was quantified. Their only tournament datapoint (published 21 Aug with Watch & Bet) is internal and self-selected: players at partner brands offering live streaming generated 44.79% higher GGR per player, 24.30% more bets and 32.53% higher average stake than players at non-streaming brands.

**BETBY Games (proprietary esports feed): GGR +32.2%**, bets +45.4%, actives +123.3% — re-accelerating from +8.43% GGR in Q3-25 and an implied ~+14% in Q2-26 (est.), but on an easy comp. GGR per active ~-41% and GGR per bet ~-9% (derived) — heavier dilution than sportsbook, pointing to cross-sold trial from the sportsbook actives surge rather than standalone demand.

**Games' mix is shrinking and is no longer disclosed.** Games was 12% of group GGR in Q1-25 and 14% in H1-25; the disclosure has not appeared since. With sportsbook out-growing Games in every subsequent period, our arithmetic puts the share near ~10% (est.). Two-year Q3 stack +43% vs sportsbook +108%.

**Product pipeline is the forward story, not the Q3 number.** SlotBets launched 8 Sep 2026 (SlotBasketball first; 15-second rounds mapped to live match events; 93–94% RTP; 20x–1,000x multipliers; iFrame-deployable in sportsbook or casino) and was showcased at SBC Summit Lisbon on 1 Oct; Watch & Bet integrated streaming went live 21 Aug; User Chat was added in-quarter. Management explicitly said these had 'limited impact' on Q3 due to timing.

**Market expansion: regulated Poland** via partnerships with Lebull and Betters — also flagged as limited Q3 impact. Poland taxes betting turnover, so a revenue-share supplier earns on a thin operator-margin base there; the contribution will be volume- rather than mix-driven (our context, not company disclosure).

**No cost, marketing or margin disclosure.** As a private supplier there is no opex, S&M % of revenue, cost-of-sales, EBITDA or cash-flow data, and no cost-transformation programme to assess. Nothing to bridge.

**Capital position: unknown.** No balance sheet, net debt, leverage or funding disclosure. Third-party databases (Tracxn) describe BETBY as unfunded/bootstrapped since 2018 — not verified by us. No buyback/dividend relevance.

**Guidance: none, old or new.** CEO Leonid Pertsovskiy's only forward comment is a qualitative aim to 'finish the year on a strong note' and that the company has 'set ambitious goals'. No numeric targets; no FY-25 or Q4-25 update was found, so the Q4 comp is undisclosed.

**Management emphasising vs burying.** Emphasised: actives +82.7% / +123.3%, 'momentum', product launches. Not disclosed: GGR base, hold, handle, NGR, partner count, client concentration, churn, and Games' share of GGR (discontinued after H1-25). The actives headline is the least informative KPI when GGR per active is falling ~27%.

**Client concentration is the unstated risk.** The 2025 base inflation (H1-25 sportsbook GGR +472%, actives +211%, bets +277%) was attributed at the time to new project launches and 'strategic clients'; growth of that shape in a B2B supplier typically rests on a handful of large operators. No top-client disclosure exists.

**Esports attribution needs care.** BETBY Games is simulated/AI-driven esports-style content, so an Esports World Cup halo accrues more naturally to their separate real-esports odds feed; the release does not separate the two, and the +123% Games actives is most plausibly distribution (new sportsbook actives exposed to the feed) rather than standalone demand.

**Thesis read-through for listed B2B comps (Kambi, Sportradar, Genius, OpenBet peers).** The update supports the view that World Cup 2026 pushed B2B volume breadth into Q3 and that esports/simulated content remains a ~10% (est.) niche adjunct. The per-player dilution is the datapoint to track: either a healthy top-of-funnel widening ahead of Q4 football density, or the first sign that incremental operator wins are smaller and lower-quality.
**Share price reaction: n/a** — no listed equity or public debt.

segments.name: Sportsbook (core B2B platform)
segments.headline: GGR +33.4% on actives +82.7%: breadth from new go-lives and tournament casuals, with GGR per active ~-27%; re-accelerating off an implied ~+24% Q2 but well below Q1's +61%, and lapping a soft-hold September 2025.
narrative: They reported sportsbook GGR up 33.4% year-on-year in Q3 2026, with the number of bets placed up 31.9% and active players across the partner network up 82.7%. The release gives no absolute GGR, no handle, no hold and no NGR, so everything below is read off those three growth rates. Read that way, the quarter was almost purely volumetric: GGR tracked bet count nearly one-for-one (GGR per bet roughly +1%), while actives grew about two-and-a-half times faster than GGR, which means GGR per active fell roughly 27% and bets per active roughly 28% by our arithmetic. The incremental player in Q3 was a lighter, lower-value player — exactly what one expects from a combination of new operator go-lives and World Cup and Esports World Cup casual sign-ups across partner brands — and nothing in the release points to deeper monetisation of the existing base.

That is a sharp change in the shape of growth. In Q3 2025 the same three KPIs were GGR +56.07%, bets +24.92% and actives +19.45%, i.e. GGR per active +31% and GGR per bet +25%, a stake- and hold-led mix; in H1 2026 (GGR +42.7%, bets +21.2%, actives +47%) GGR per bet was still +18% while GGR per active had only just turned negative at -3%. Q3 2026 is therefore the first period in which per-player economics are visibly diluting. We would not over-read a single quarter — a tournament-heavy July with knockout-stage football and the Esports World Cup running into August is precisely when casual breadth should peak — but the direction needs to reverse in Q4 for the actives headline to mean much, and the company gives no cohort or retention data with which to judge it.

On trajectory, sportsbook GGR growth has stepped down from +61% in Q1 (a record March) to +42.7% for H1 and +33.4% in Q3. The company does not publish Q2 standalone, but equal-weighting the Q1 and Q2 2025 bases implies Q2 2026 growth of only ~24% (roughly 20–30% depending on base weights; our estimate), so Q3 is in fact a modest re-acceleration off the Q2 trough rather than a continued fade — and that Q2 softness is itself notable given the World Cup group stage sat in June. Two points on the comparison base matter. First, the Q3 2025 release flagged lower sportsbook margins in September 2025 from unfavourable sporting results, so part of this quarter's +33.4% is hold normalisation that the company cannot separate for us. Second, Q3 2025 was not event-free either: they cited a 743% GGR surge in pre-match markets during the FIFA Club World Cup, whose final fell on 13 July 2025. The two-year Q3 stack is still ~+108%, which is the more honest measure of scale gained.

Management attributed the quarter to the concluding stages of the FIFA World Cup (the knockout rounds through the 19 July final), the Esports World Cup, and strong activity across the operator network, but quantified none of it: there is no World Cup GGR, handle, actives or margin datapoint, and no comparison to any prior tournament. The only tournament data they have published came with the 21 August Watch & Bet launch, claiming that players at partner brands with live streaming generated 44.79% higher GGR per player, placed 24.30% more bets and staked 32.53% more on average than players at brands without streaming during the tournament. That is a self-selected comparison — streaming brands are likely the larger, better-resourced operators — and should be treated as a product-marketing claim rather than an uplift estimate. Handle, net hold, structural margin, parlay mix and promotional intensity as a share of handle are not disclosed in any period, so the volume-versus-price-versus-luck split that would normally anchor a sportsbook note cannot be made here.

The forward-looking content is product and market expansion, all of it explicitly flagged as having limited impact on Q3 because of timing. SlotBets launched on 8 September — SlotBasketball first, with 15-second betting rounds split into three five-second windows that each record the highest-value live event, a 93–94% RTP, multipliers from 20x to 1,000x, and iFrame deployment inside either a sportsbook or a casino lobby — and was given a dedicated press conference at SBC Summit Lisbon on 1 October with a stated intention to extend the format to other sports. Watch & Bet integrated streaming went live on 21 August and User Chat was added in-quarter. On markets, they entered regulated Poland through partnerships with Lebull and Betters; Poland taxes betting turnover, so a revenue-share supplier earns off a thin operator margin there and the contribution will be volume- rather than mix-driven (our context). No partner count, go-live count, client-concentration or churn figures were given, and the 2025 base inflation (H1 2025 sportsbook GGR +472%, actives +211%, attributed at the time to new project launches and strategic clients) points to a concentrated client book. There is no segment guidance; the CEO's only forward comment is a qualitative aim to finish the year strongly.

segments.name: BETBY Games (proprietary esports feed)
segments.headline: GGR +32.2% on actives +123.3% and bets +45.4%: a re-acceleration on an easy +8.4% comp, but GGR per active ~-41% and a shrinking (~10% est.) share of group GGR that the company no longer discloses.
narrative: BETBY Games, the proprietary esports-style feed embedded in the sportsbook front-end, reported GGR +32.2%, bets +45.4% and actives +123.3% year-on-year. The dilution here is heavier than in the core book: GGR per active roughly -41%, bets per active roughly -35% and GGR per bet roughly -9% by our arithmetic. Actives more than doubling while GGR per active falls by two-fifths reads as cross-sold trial — the +82.7% sportsbook active surge being exposed to Games content inside the same product — rather than standalone demand. Management grouped the Esports World Cup among the quarter's drivers, but since BETBY Games is simulated, AI-driven content rather than real-match esports, any EWC halo accrues more naturally to their separate real-esports odds feed; the release does not separate the two and no Games-specific event data was given.

The comp was easy. Q3 2025 was the segment's weakest quarter in the disclosed series (GGR +8.43%, bets +6.18%, actives +11.85%), and the content line-up was broadened with eKabaddi, eVolleyball and eBoxing in September 2025, so Q3 2026 carried a full year of the expanded portfolio against a base that lacked it. On trajectory, Games GGR growth went +42% in Q1, +28% for H1 — implying ~+14% in Q2 on equal base weights (est.) — and now +32.2%: a genuine re-acceleration, but the two-year Q3 stack is only ~+43% against ~+108% for sportsbook, and in H1 2026 GGR per bet was still +11.5% whereas Q3 flipped to -9%, so the product is now also being bet in smaller tickets.

Mix is drifting down and the company has stopped telling us by how much. Games was 12% of group GGR in Q1 2025 and 14% in H1 2025; that disclosure has not appeared since, and with sportsbook out-growing Games in every subsequent period our arithmetic puts the share near ~10% (est., assuming the 14% held in the Q3 2024 base). The segment remains a useful engagement and differentiation tool for operators in dead periods of the real-sport calendar — and it is the content most exposed to the 'younger, digitally native' positioning management used for SlotBets at SBC Lisbon — but at this scale it is not the growth engine the 2025 releases framed it as. No Games-specific guidance, pricing, operator-adoption or content-roadmap figures were given.

highlights.text: **Widest top-of-funnel in the disclosed series:** sportsbook actives +82.7% and Games actives +123.3% YoY, with bets +31.9% / +45.4%; two-year Q3 sportsbook GGR stack ~+108%.

**Re-acceleration off the Q2 trough:** Q3 sportsbook GGR +33.4% vs an implied ~+24% in Q2 (est.) — the World Cup knockouts and Esports World Cup did lift volume into Q3 after a surprisingly soft group-stage quarter.
**BETBY Games re-accelerated to +32.2% GGR** from +8.43% in Q3-25 and ~+14% implied Q2-26 (est.), with bets +45.4% — the expanded content line-up (eKabaddi, eVolleyball, eBoxing) now in the base.

**Product cadence is genuinely differentiated:** SlotBets (8 Sep; a new 'slotbetting' category bridging casino and sportsbook UX, 15-second live-data rounds, 93–94% RTP), Watch & Bet streaming (21 Aug) and User Chat all shipped in one quarter, with management explicitly positioning them as Q4/2027 drivers.
**Regulated-market expansion:** entry into Poland via Lebull and Betters adds a licensed European footprint to the MGA B2B base, with contribution still to come.

**Streaming uplift data** (44.79% higher GGR per player, +24.30% bets, +32.53% average stake at streaming-enabled brands during the World Cup) gives operators a commercial case for Watch & Bet — caveat self-selection.

lowlights.text: **Per-player dilution:** implied sportsbook GGR per active ~-27% and Games ~-41% (our arithmetic) — growth is breadth, not monetisation; no cohort or retention data to judge whether the World Cup intake sticks.
**Deceleration:** sportsbook GGR growth +61% (Q1) → +42.7% (H1) → +33.4% (Q3); the implied Q2 at ~+24% (est.) means the World Cup group stage did not produce a step-change.
**Soft comp:** Q3-25 carried a weak-hold September; part of the +33.4% is normalisation. With no handle, hold or NGR disclosure, luck cannot be separated from structural growth.

**Disclosure quality is poor and getting thinner:** no monetary figures in any period, Games' share of GGR discontinued after H1-25, no Q2 standalone, no Q4-25/FY-25 update found, no partner count, no client concentration.

**Esports attribution is loose:** the Esports World Cup is cited as a driver, but BETBY Games is simulated content; the +123% actives looks like distribution via the sportsbook rather than standalone demand, and Games' mix has likely slipped to ~10% (est.).

**Concentration risk unquantified:** the 2025 base (H1-25 GGR +472%, actives +211%) was built on 'strategic clients' and new launches; a B2B book of that shape can swing on one or two operator decisions, and no churn or top-client data is given.

forecast.intro: There is no guidance to bridge — BETBY has never issued numeric targets, and the only forward statement in the Q3 release is CEO Leonid Pertsovskiy's qualitative aim to 'finish the year on a strong note'. The bridge below is therefore our reconstruction of the 2026 growth path for the division that matters (sportsbook, ~90% of GGR by our estimate), using the company's reported Q1, H1 and Q3 YoY rates and an equal-weight assumption for the undisclosed Q2 base. The moving parts for Q4 are: a dense European club-football calendar with no tournament comp issue (Q4-25 had none either, though the Q4-25 rate itself was never published); first contributions from Poland (Lebull, Betters), SlotBets and Watch & Bet, all small at this stage; and the retention of the Q3 casual intake, which is the swing factor for the actives line.

forecast.view: **Revenue:** we expect Q4-26 sportsbook GGR growth of roughly **+25–35% YoY (est.)** and BETBY Games of **+20–35% (est.)**, which would put full-year 2026 sportsbook GGR growth in the **high-30s% (est.)** given Q1 +61%, implied Q2 ~+24% and Q3 +33.4% (quarter weights unknown). The skew is to the downside of that range if GGR per active keeps falling at -25% or worse while actives growth fades as World Cup cohorts churn; the skew is upside only if Q3's active intake proves sticky into the club-football season. Note that BETBY's own revenue is a revenue share on operator NGR plus fees, so **BETBY revenue growth should run below partner GGR growth** wherever new clients come in on ramp pricing, promotional intensity is high, or taxes bite (Poland's turnover tax is the obvious example). **Margin and leverage:** n/a — nothing is disclosed and we will not model what cannot be checked; a bootstrapped supplier growing partner GGR ~2x in two years is, however, a natural strategic target, and a funding or M&A event is a more plausible 2027 catalyst than any disclosed financial milestone. **Disclosure:** the single most useful thing management could do is publish an absolute GGR base, a hold metric and partner counts; until then every print is a momentum signal only.
watch: Q4-26 / FY-26 trading update (no Q4-25 or FY-25 release was found — whether a year-end print appears, and whether it finally carries absolute GGR, hold or partner-count figures).
Direction of implied GGR per active and bets per active: dilution of ~-27% needs to narrow in Q4 for the +82.7% actives to be read as franchise growth rather than tournament churn.
Whether the Games share-of-GGR disclosure is reinstated; our ~10% estimate assumes no Games-specific wins.
Poland ramp: go-live timing for Lebull and Betters, and any further regulated-market licences (BETBY operates on an MGA B2B licence).
SlotBets adoption: number of operators live, extension beyond SlotBasketball, and any regulatory classification questions (RNG-free slot mechanics in sportsbook lobbies).
Client concentration and churn: any named operator migrating in-house or to a rival; the 2025 'strategic client' base is the key fragility.
Hold normalisation: September–October football results and whether management again flags margin effects, which would confirm Q3's comp benefit.
Corporate: funding round, strategic investor or acquisition — the most likely route to real financial disclosure.

No monetary figures exist: all revenue/EBITDA/EPS/cash/debt lines are n/a, not estimated; FX conversion is therefore not applicable (no reporting currency disclosed; functional currency presumed EUR as a Malta entity). Derived per-active/per-bet metrics, two-year stacks, the implied Q2-26 growth (~+24% sportsbook, ~+14% Games; equal-weight base assumption, range ~20–30%) and the ~10% Games share are our arithmetic. Fiscal year-end 31 Dec is inferred from calendar-quarter reporting, not from filings; no statutory accounts were accessible. No Q4-25/FY-25 update was found — it may not exist. Tracxn's 'unfunded' status and third-party office/partner-count claims are unverified and not relied upon. The user-supplied Yogonet and Focus GN URLs could not be fetched (not accessible); their headlines (33.4%) were corroborated via search-index snippets only.
